text.p: Finnish insurer Vakuutusosakeyhtio Pohjola said in a statement on Thursday it would buy the stock of Salama from its associate Suomi and planned to take over Suomi's life-insurance portfolio later.
It also said current president Iiro Viinanen would also become CEO.

A company official at a news conference confirmed that the restructuring was in effect a concentration of the group's life-insurance operations into its public part Vakuutusosakeyhtio Pohjola, which will be renamed Pohjola-Yhtyma or group.
"Pohjola group's life-insurance will be concentrated in the public part of the group," the official said.
"The new structure will secure the competitiveness of life insurance and serve clients' interests in the rapidly growing markets," Pojhjola said in a statement.
"This is expected to have a positive impact on the share price," Viinanen told the news conference.

"The public company Pohjola will become a holding company, Pohjola Group Ltd. Pohjola's insurance business will be transferred to Pohjola Non-life, a non-life insurance company to be established," Pohjola said.

Suomi will continue to manage the existing insurance portfolio and the premiums written pertaining to that portfolio, but it would be transferred to Pohjola Life "at a later stage," it said, but gave no timetable.
An external board of directors will be appointed for the new public Pohjola group while the supervisory boards of Pohjola, Eurooppalainen and Salama will be abolished, it said.

The arrangements will not lead to any changes for pension group Ilmarinen. "The new structure will secure the competitiveness of life assurance and serve clients' interests in the rapidly growing markets," Pohjola said.

"Pohjola's strong financial standing can, within the framework of the new structure, be directed toward underwriting life assurance business, which will produce added value for Pohjola's shareholders," it said.
Effective July 1, Pirkko Alitalo, senior vice president, will become executive vice president. She will remain in charge of the companies' investments.
Current CEO Jukka Rantala was named Senior Vice President/Research and will also be in charge also of investor relations.
